leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight files include base editing in their preferred configuration, the broadest explicit support on the table, but in different shapes: Aqvist and Chabes put it first, while Linke and Somfai use it as a second part beside B039. Laureate sets differ: Liu alone (Aqvist, Chabes in the file, Linke, Somfai) versus Liu, Komor and Gaudelli (Chabes in his round-1 response text and opening proposal). All four flag the same reservations: the method is about ten years old, clinical outcomes are still accumulating, the independent Kondo and Nishida deaminase-fusion work is unresolved by a Liu-only citation, and the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize may make it read as an extension of genome editing. Daniel Aili lists B062 only as an alternative, so he is not counted as a supporter.

Two files propose the identical two-part prize: Buchwald and Hartwig for Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling plus Liu for base editing. They share the rationale of pairing a core molecule-making method with a chemical-biology tool, and both concede that nothing scientifically links the two parts. They differ in emphasis on the weak points: Linke highlights the Kosugi and Migita-type priority question, Somfai the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo credit. No other member lists B039 in a preferred configuration.

Targeted protein degradation is the sole prize in Aili's file and the second part of Aqvist's. They agree on the concept (PROTACs, cereblon-mediated molecular glues) but not on the trio: Aili names Crews, Deshaies and Handa, while Aqvist names Crews and Handa only; Aili says he would accept Ciulli in place of Deshaies. Both note that no bifunctional degrader appears to be approved, though the molecular-glue branch is in the clinic.

Aqvist alone proposes base editing (Liu) and degradation (Crews, Handa) as a two-part prize, arguing that each part keeps attribution clean within three names. Others see base editing alone, degradation alone, or base editing paired with C-N coupling; B066 appears as an alternative in the files of Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai and Chabes.

Sparr alone puts biomolecular condensates (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as the whole prize, on a physical-chemical concept argument. She flags that Pappu and Mittag fall outside a three-name cut and that her own field proximity may inflate her view. B036 is an alternative for Aqvist and Chabes and for Linke.

Brzezinski alone proposes nitrogenase (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt) for structure and mechanism. He concedes the catalytic mechanism at the cofactor is still debated and that credit is spread over at least five people.

Zou alone proposes zeolite and molecular-sieve design (Corma, Davis, Zones). He notes that no other member ranked B033 in an opening top eight, that it is a broad programme rather than one discovery, and that his field proximity may inflate his view.

areas_of_agreement: Base editing (B062) is the candidate most often present in preferred configurations (Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Somfai), and every one of those four calls it a chemically conceived capability with independent validation and clinical uptake.

Every member who discusses base editing names Kondo and Nishida's independent deaminase-fusion work as a real complication for attribution, and several members treat the age of the field as a maturity concern.

All eight members apply some version of a new-capability and clear-principle test, and all eight state a concrete reservation about their own first choice, so no first choice is presented as uncontested.
Nobody argues that a three-person limit comfortably fits their own preferred field: Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Sparr and Zou each state that credited contributors are left out by the cut.
Targeted protein degradation (B066) is a recurring second option: it is Aili's first choice, a part of Aqvist's configuration, and an alternative for Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Sparr.
scientific_disputes: Is base editing chemistry or protein engineering and genome biology? Aqvist, Chabes and Linke call it chemical; Somfai and Aili stress the protein-engineering content; the evolved TadA deaminase is cited by Chabes as real enzyme chemistry.

Is Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B039) a new principle or a refinement of the cross-coupling paradigm honoured in 2010? Linke and Somfai see a distinct mechanism-guided ligand-design advance; Sparr ranks it sixth and Zou and Linke note the overlap.

Is targeted protein degradation chiefly a chemical design principle (Aili) or a pharmacology and medicine topic (risk noted by Aili)? Is the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism the same discovery as the PROTAC concept?
Do condensates (B036) have a secure core concept (Sparr) when physiological relevance and the liquid-versus-gel character of many condensates are still contested, and is it chemistry or cell biology?
Is nitrogenase (B012) mature enough when the catalytic mechanism at the cofactor, including the E4 hydride state and N2 binding site, is still debated (Brzezinski himself)?
Is zeolite design (B033) a single citable discovery or a broad research programme (Zou)?
attribution_disputes: B062: Liu alone (Aqvist, Chabes in his file, Linke, Somfai) versus adding Komor and Gaudelli (Chabes's opening proposal and response text, Somfai's discussion) versus the unresolved Kondo and Nishida claim.

B066: Crews, Deshaies and Handa (Aili) versus Crews and Handa (Aqvist); Aqvist's file also credits Ciulli's structural work, Aili would accept Ciulli in place of Deshaies, and Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are named as excluded contributors.

B039: Buchwald and Hartwig as a clean pair (Linke, Somfai) with Kosugi as a precursor whose stoichiometric tin-amide work the files treat differently (Linke raises a Kosugi and Migita-type priority question, Somfai calls Kosugi a precursor, not the general method).
B036: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-grammar work Sparr says gives the picture its predictive power.
B012: Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt leave out Dean and Ribbe and the genetics and cofactor-biosynthesis line (Brzezinski).
B033: Corma, Davis and Zones leave out Tsapatsis and Yu (Zou).
maturity_disputes: Base editing dates from 2016-2017 and clinical outcomes are still accumulating (Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Somfai; Zou's remarks about recognition being early appear in Aili's response); the position has to be weighed against its reproducibility across many laboratories.
No bifunctional degrader appears to be approved, although the molecular-glue branch is established in medicine (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes).
C-N coupling is mature (about two decades of use) but is sometimes seen as late or derivative rather than as unrecognised (Somfai says overdue; Linke and Somfai concede the 2010 overlap).
Nitrogenase is mature structurally but open mechanistically (Brzezinski); condensates have more than a decade of confirmation but contested physiology (Sparr).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Sparr discloses that her own field proximity (soft matter, lipid-protein co-assembly, amyloid) could lead her to overweight condensates (B036).
Zou discloses that his own field proximity (zeolites and porous frameworks) may inflate his view of B033.

No member discloses a personal, collaborative or institutional conflict with a credited candidate; the chair notes that he is himself an explicit supporter of the B039 plus B062 configuration and that he is a physicist chairing a chemistry committee.
questions_for_round2: For B062: should the citation name Liu alone, Liu with Komor and Gaudelli, or include Kondo and Nishida, and what dated primary evidence separates the Komor and Gaudelli first demonstrations from the Nishida and Kondo work?

Is a one-part prize (B062, B066, B036, B012 or B033) or a two-part prize (B039 plus B062, or B062 plus B066) preferred, and can the members proposing a two-part prize name a unifying citation or accept that none exists?

For B039: does the 2010 cross-coupling prize leave Pd-catalysed C-N coupling a distinct and unrecognised principle, and how should the Kosugi and Migita-type precedents be placed chronologically relative to Buchwald and Hartwig?

For B066: are PROTAC design and cereblon-based molecular glues one discovery for a single citation, and should the third name be Deshaies or Ciulli, given that no bifunctional degrader appears approved?
Which members who list B062 or B066 only as an alternative (Aili, Brzezinski, Sparr, Zou) would move them into a preferred configuration, and under what citation and laureate set?

For the single-supporter positions B012, B033 and B036: what evidence of independent confirmation and attribution would persuade at least four further members, given that B033 has no opening top-eight rank from another member?

Please clarify the record: Somfai's response says the chair ranked nanopore sequencing second, whereas the chair's round-1 alternatives are B066 and B036; round 2 should state which ballot ID is intended.
summary.chair_observation: Explicit preferences are split across six distinct ballot IDs in eight files, with B062 appearing in four files and no configuration yet having more than two explicit supporters. No position reaches the five-member majority on the stated preferences, so round 2 needs to establish whether the B062 supporters can agree on one laureate set and whether the second part of a two-part prize is B039, B066 or none.
